files.setup.sql:
-- =====================================================================
--  setup.sql -- builds the practice database used in the whole bible
--
--  From the labs/ folder, run:
--      duckdb practice.duckdb < setup.sql
--  You can run it again at any time to reset the data.
-- =====================================================================

create schema if not exists jaffle_shop;   -- the shop's application data
create schema if not exists stripe;        -- the payment provider's data

create or replace table jaffle_shop.customers as
select * from read_csv('data/customers.csv', header = true,
    columns = {'id': 'INTEGER', 'first_name': 'VARCHAR', 'last_name': 'VARCHAR',
               'email': 'VARCHAR', 'country': 'VARCHAR', 'signup_date': 'DATE'});

create or replace table jaffle_shop.orders as
select * from read_csv('data/orders.csv', header = true,
    columns = {'id': 'INTEGER', 'user_id': 'INTEGER', 'order_date': 'DATE',
               'status': 'VARCHAR', '_loaded_at': 'TIMESTAMP'});

create or replace table jaffle_shop.order_items as
select * from read_csv('data/order_items.csv', header = true,
    columns = {'id': 'INTEGER', 'order_id': 'INTEGER', 'product_id': 'INTEGER',
               'quantity': 'INTEGER'});

create or replace table jaffle_shop.products as
select * from read_csv('data/products.csv', header = true,
    columns = {'id': 'INTEGER', 'name': 'VARCHAR', 'category': 'VARCHAR',
               'price_cents': 'INTEGER'});

create or replace table stripe.payments as
select * from read_csv('data/payments.csv', header = true,
    columns = {'id': 'INTEGER', 'orderid': 'INTEGER', 'paymentmethod': 'VARCHAR',
               'status': 'VARCHAR', 'amount': 'INTEGER', 'created': 'DATE',
               '_loaded_at': 'TIMESTAMP'});

-- quick check: one row per table with its row count
select 'jaffle_shop.customers' as table_name, count(*) as n_rows from jaffle_shop.customers
union all select 'jaffle_shop.orders', count(*) from jaffle_shop.orders
union all select 'jaffle_shop.order_items', count(*) from jaffle_shop.order_items
union all select 'jaffle_shop.products', count(*) from jaffle_shop.products
union all select 'stripe.payments', count(*) from stripe.payments;
files.updates/README.md:
# Data update scripts

These scripts change the RAW tables of the practice database (`jaffle_shop.*` and `stripe.*`)
to simulate new loads. They never touch the schemas created by dbt.

| Script | Used in | What it simulates |
|---|---|---|
| `day2.sql` | Chapter 13 (snapshots), Chapter 14 (incremental models, microbatch), later chapters | the next loading day (2 January 2026): changed rows + new rows |
| `fresh_load.sql` | Chapter 21 (source freshness) | 2 orders loaded "right now", so that `dbt source freshness` passes |

## How to run them

Copy the folder next to your database once, then run a script with the DuckDB CLI
(close every other DuckDB session first: DuckDB allows only one writer, and even a
`duckdb -readonly` session blocks dbt and these scripts):

```bash
cp -r ~/Documents/Adnane/dbt-bible/labs/updates ~/dbt-course/practice/
cd ~/dbt-course/practice
duckdb practice.duckdb < updates/day2.sql
duckdb practice.duckdb < updates/fresh_load.sql
```

Without the DuckDB CLI (same statements, run by the Python duckdb library):

```bash
python tools/build_practice_db.py ~/dbt-course/practice/practice.duckdb --sql labs/updates/day2.sql
```

Each script ends with a small check query (row counts, or the newest `_loaded_at`).

## Reset

To go back to the original data (day 1), re-run setup.sql. It recreates the 5 raw tables
(`create or replace table`) and does NOT drop the dbt schemas:

```bash
cd ~/dbt-course/practice
duckdb practice.duckdb < setup.sql
```

Warning: after a reset, do not run `dbt snapshot` (or a full `dbt build`) before you apply
day2.sql again, otherwise the snapshots record the reset as a change.

## day2.sql in detail (deterministic, safe to run twice)

Customers (5 rows changed, no new rows):

| id | change |
|---|---|
| 5 | country Morocco -> France |
| 12 | country Morocco -> Spain |
| 40 | country Spain -> Germany |
| 17 | email NULL -> `leo.fernandez17@example.com` |
| 11 | email `YOUSSEF.WILSON11@EXAMPLE.COM` -> `youssef.wilson11@example.com` (case fix only) |

Orders: 13 rows changed, each with a new `_loaded_at` on 2026-01-02 (07:00 to 08:00):
the 10 `placed` orders (288, 289, 290, 292, 295, 296, 297, 298, 299, 300) become `shipped`;
orders 255, 276, 291 go from `shipped` to `completed`.
20 new orders (ids 301-320), dated 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-04 (5 per day), `_loaded_at` the same day;
301-310 `completed`, 311-320 `shipped`. Customers 96 and 97 (who never ordered) place orders 301 and 306.

Order items: 32 new rows (ids 607-638) for the new orders.

Payments: 30 new successful payments (ids 342-371), amounts in cents equal to the total of the
order's items: 342-361 for the new orders (created on the order date), 362-371 for the 10 formerly
placed orders (created 2026-01-02).

### Counts before / after (verified)

| Table / measure | day 1 (setup.sql) | after day2.sql | after day2.sql + 1 x fresh_load.sql |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| jaffle_shop.customers | 100 | 100 (5 changed) | 100 |
| jaffle_shop.orders | 300 | 320 (13 changed, 20 new) | 322 |
| jaffle_shop.order_items | 606 | 638 | 640 |
| jaffle_shop.products | 12 | 12 | 12 |
| stripe.payments | 341 | 371 | 373 |
| successful payments | 317 | 347 | 349 |
| total successful amount (cents) | 500440 | 544320 | 545140 (*) |
| max(orders._loaded_at) | 2025-12-31 16:22 | 2026-01-04 16:13 | the current UTC time |
| orders by status | completed 239, shipped 21, returned 18, return_pending 12, placed 10 | completed 252, shipped 38, returned 18, return_pending 12, placed 0 | + 2 completed |
| customers with NULL email / upper-case email | 5 / 9 | 4 / 8 | 4 / 8 |
| customers without orders | 11 | 9 | 9 |
| orphan orders (user_id without customer) | 1 (order 159) | 1 | 1 |

(*) fresh_load.sql adds 380 + 440 cents (1 Cappuccino for customer 1, 2 Croissants for customer 2).

Effect on the dbt project (reference run, logs of Chapters 13 and 14):
`customers_snapshot` 100 -> 105 rows (5 closed versions), `orders_snapshot` 300 -> 333 rows
(13 closed versions, 20 new orders), incremental `fct_orders` 300 -> 320 rows (33 rows processed:
13 updated + 20 inserted), `fct_monthly_revenue` 65 -> 71 rows.

## fresh_load.sql in detail (NOT idempotent)

Adds 2 orders (ids = current max + 1 and + 2), one item each, one successful payment each,
with `_loaded_at` = the current time in UTC (`current_timestamp at time zone 'UTC'`).
`_loaded_at` has no time zone; dbt treats such values as UTC when it computes freshness,
so storing the UTC time keeps the freshness age correct whatever the computer's time zone.
Every run adds 2 more orders.

-- =====================================================================
--  day2.sql -- "the next loading day" for the practice database
--
--  It simulates what the source systems send on 2 January 2026:
--    * jaffle_shop.customers : 5 customers change (3 move to another
--                              country, 1 NULL email gets a value,
--                              1 email is rewritten in lower case)
--    * jaffle_shop.orders    : the 10 'placed' orders become 'shipped',
--                              3 'shipped' orders become 'completed'
--                              (every changed row gets a new _loaded_at
--                              on 2026-01-02), and 20 NEW orders
--                              (ids 301-320, 2026-01-01 .. 2026-01-04)
--    * jaffle_shop.order_items : 32 new items (ids 607-638) for the
--                              new orders
--    * stripe.payments       : 30 new successful payments (ids 342-371):
--                              20 for the new orders, 10 for the orders
--                              that were 'placed' (created 2026-01-02)
--
--  From your practice folder (DuckDB CLI closed everywhere else):
--      duckdb practice.duckdb < updates/day2.sql
--
--  The script is safe to run twice: updates write the same values again
--  and inserts skip ids that already exist.
--  To go back to the original data, re-run setup.sql.
-- =====================================================================

begin transaction;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. customers: 5 changed rows
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
update jaffle_shop.customers as c
set country = v.new_country
from (values
    (5,  'France'),     -- was Morocco
    (12, 'Spain'),      -- was Morocco
    (40, 'Germany')     -- was Spain
) as v(id, new_country)
where c.id = v.id;

-- a customer who had no email gives one
update jaffle_shop.customers
set email = 'leo.fernandez17@example.com'
where id = 17;          -- was NULL

-- a customer fixes the case of their email
update jaffle_shop.customers
set email = 'youssef.wilson11@example.com'
where id = 11;          -- was YOUSSEF.WILSON11@EXAMPLE.COM

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. orders: 13 changed rows (new status + new _loaded_at)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
update jaffle_shop.orders as o
set status = v.new_status,
    _loaded_at = v.new_loaded_at
from (values
    -- the 10 'placed' orders are now shipped
    (288, 'shipped',   timestamp '2026-01-02 07:00:00'),
    (289, 'shipped',   timestamp '2026-01-02 07:05:00'),
    (290, 'shipped',   timestamp '2026-01-02 07:10:00'),
    (292, 'shipped',   timestamp '2026-01-02 07:15:00'),
    (295, 'shipped',   timestamp '2026-01-02 07:20:00'),
    (296, 'shipped',   timestamp '2026-01-02 07:25:00'),
    (297, 'shipped',   timestamp '2026-01-02 07:30:00'),
    (298, 'shipped',   timestamp '2026-01-02 07:35:00'),
    (299, 'shipped',   timestamp '2026-01-02 07:40:00'),
    (300, 'shipped',   timestamp '2026-01-02 07:45:00'),
    -- 3 shipped orders are now completed
    (255, 'completed', timestamp '2026-01-02 07:50:00'),
    (276, 'completed', timestamp '2026-01-02 07:55:00'),
    (291, 'completed', timestamp '2026-01-02 08:00:00')
) as v(id, new_status, new_loaded_at)
where o.id = v.id;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. orders: 20 new orders (ids 301-320)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
insert into jaffle_shop.orders (id, user_id, order_date, status, _loaded_at)
select * from (values
    (301, 96, date '2026-01-01', 'completed', timestamp '2026-01-01 08:00:00'),
    (302,  5, date '2026-01-01', 'completed', timestamp '2026-01-01 10:07:00'),

-- =====================================================================
--  fresh_load.sql -- "data arrived a moment ago"
--
--  Adds 2 small new orders (with their items and successful payments)
--  whose _loaded_at is the current time. Use it when you want
--  `dbt source freshness` to report PASS (Chapter 21).
--
--  From your practice folder (DuckDB CLI closed everywhere else):
--      duckdb practice.duckdb < updates/fresh_load.sql
--
--  Unlike day2.sql, every run adds 2 MORE orders: the new ids are
--  "current max id + 1" and "current max id + 2".
--  To go back to the original data, re-run setup.sql.
--
--  Why "at time zone 'UTC'"? _loaded_at has no time zone (TIMESTAMP).
--  dbt reads such values as UTC when it computes the age of the data,
--  so we store the current UTC time, whatever your computer's time zone.
-- =====================================================================

begin transaction;

-- the batch to load: 2 orders, 1 item each, 1 payment each
create temp table fresh_batch as
select
    (select max(id) from jaffle_shop.orders) + v.n       as order_id,
    v.user_id,
    (select max(id) from jaffle_shop.order_items) + v.n  as order_item_id,
    v.product_id,
    v.quantity,
    (select max(id) from stripe.payments) + v.n          as payment_id,
    cast(current_timestamp at time zone 'UTC' as timestamp) as loaded_at
from (values
    (1, 1, 2, 1),       -- customer 1 buys 1 Cappuccino
    (2, 2, 7, 2)        -- customer 2 buys 2 Croissants
) as v(n, user_id, product_id, quantity);

insert into jaffle_shop.orders (id, user_id, order_date, status, _loaded_at)
select order_id, user_id, cast(loaded_at as date), 'completed', loaded_at
from fresh_batch;

insert into jaffle_shop.order_items (id, order_id, product_id, quantity)
select order_item_id, order_id, product_id, quantity
from fresh_batch;

insert into stripe.payments (id, orderid, paymentmethod, status, amount, created, _loaded_at)
select
    b.payment_id,
    b.order_id,
    'credit_card',
    'success',
    b.quantity * p.price_cents,        -- amount in CENTS = the item total
    cast(b.loaded_at as date),
    b.loaded_at
from fresh_batch as b
inner join jaffle_shop.products as p
    on p.id = b.product_id;

drop table fresh_batch;

commit;

-- quick check: the newest load time per table with a _loaded_at column
select 'jaffle_shop.orders' as table_name, count(*) as n_rows, max(_loaded_at) as max_loaded_at
from jaffle_shop.orders
union all
select 'stripe.payments', count(*), max(_loaded_at)
from stripe.payments;
